turns.doctor_question: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: Well, I came in because... I just can’t seem to get anything in order anymore. It's like my whole life is in piles. My kitchen table, oh, you should see it, it's just covered with my husband’s appointment papers—he had that knee replacement last year, you know, the one where they keep you in the hospital for three days? The food was awful, he complained the whole time. But anyway, there's his papers, and church flyers, notes from the senior center... I help out with the bake sale there, though nobody buys my fruitcake anymore, which is a shame because it's my grandmother's recipe. She used to soak it in rum for a month. But I just sit at that table, looking at all these half-finished lists, and I don't know which thing to do first. I just stare at it all, and before I know it, the whole day is gone. I don't know where the time goes. It feels like the clock is just spinning and I haven't even started on the laundry.

symptom_reasoning.S005: The patient explicitly states she cannot get anything in order, her life is in piles, and she struggles to organize her tasks and half-finished lists.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangential speech, wandering off-topic to discuss her husband's knee surgery, hospital food, and a fruitcake recipe before returning to her point.
symptom_reasoning.S031: The patient demonstrates indecisiveness, stating she sits at the table not knowing which task to do first until the entire day has passed.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find it distressing or difficult to throw any of those papers and items away?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, no, it's not that. I don't mind throwing things out at all. I really don't. If someone handed me a garbage bag right now, I'd happily toss most of it. We actually had to switch to those really thick black bags, you know, the heavy-duty ones? Because the raccoons in our neighborhood have just gotten so bold lately. Just last week, Arthur—my husband—woke up at two in the morning because they were making an absolute racket out by the garage. He went out there in his robe with a broom to chase them off, which is just ridiculous with his bad knee, I told him he was going to fall and end up right back in the hospital. 

But anyway, the recycling company changed the rules on us again, too. Now you have to separate the cardboard from the glossy paper, and who has the time to sit there and figure out if a church flyer is glossy or just... smooth? So no, I don't care about keeping the papers, I just... I look at the pile and I can't figure out how to start sorting it all for the bins, so they just stay on the table.

turns.doctor_question: When did you first start noticing this kind of trouble with organizing and getting things done?
turns.patient_response: Well, let's see... it really got bad, like this bad, about a year and three months ago. That was right around the time Arthur started needing so much help with his appointments and his daily schedule. You know, before that, he used to handle all his own driving and scheduling. He was so proud of that Buick of his. It’s a LeSabre, 2004, but he kept it looking like it just rolled off the lot. He used to wash it every Sunday morning before church, using this special wax he ordered from a catalog. He wouldn't let me or anyone else touch it. But then his knee gave out, and he couldn't press the brake pedal down hard enough anymore. We had a real scare one afternoon when he almost backed into Mrs. Gable's prized hydrangeas across the street. She would have had a fit, she wins the garden club ribbon every single year and she never lets anyone forget it. So I had to take over all his arrangements and driving, and... well, ever since then, it's just been a year and three months of me not being able to keep my head above water with all the organizing.

symptom_reasoning.S005: The patient explicitly states she has been unable to 'keep my head above water with all the organizing' since taking over her husband's arrangements a year and three months ago.

turns.doctor_question: Looking back to when you were younger, such as during school or earlier in your adulthood, did you ever have trouble with staying organized or focusing on tasks?
turns.patient_response:
Well, you know, it's funny you ask that. I was just thinking about my old school days the other week. I ran into Maryellen at the grocery store—she was in my third-grade class, if you can believe it. She still has that same curly red hair, though I'm sure it's out of a bottle now. We were talking about our old teacher, Mrs. Higgins. She was a terror, absolute terror. She used to make us sit with our hands folded on our desks if we finished early. 

But, oh, to answer your question... yes, I suppose I did have trouble. Even when I was a little girl, my teachers always wrote on my report cards that I was bright but, well, careless. I was always forgetting my books or my homework assignments. My mother used to get so frustrated, she’d say I’d lose my head if it wasn't attached. And Mrs. Higgins, she always had to remind me to finish my seatwork. I’d be looking out the window, watching the older boys play kickball, and she'd tap my desk with her ruler and tell me I couldn't go outside for recess until my math was done. Kickball was so popular back then, Arthur used to play it too, though of course that was long before his knee went bad...
